source.title: Junior School Curriculum Design: Social Studies, Grade 9
source.publisher: cbcelimu.com (mirror of KICD design; KICD's own Google Drive copy, file ID 1gMXIzQnV-F1a7n_dJ82QU2-BTtw3B-NW, is owner-blocked for direct download)
source.notes: Fetched the PDF directly from the cbcelimu.com mirror; WebFetch's own summarizer failed to extract text ('unable to extract text'), but it had saved the PDF locally, and the Read tool parsed the full 71-page document natively. All strand/sub-strand headings, specific learning outcomes, and key inquiry questions below were read verbatim from that extracted text, not summarized by an intermediate model. Title-match verification: the PDF's own title page reads 'KENYA INSTITUTE OF CURRICULUM DEVELOPMENT ... JUNIOR SCHOOL CURRICULUM DESIGN SOCIAL STUDIES GRADE 9', ISBN 978-9914-43-949-4, 'First published 2024', published/printed by KICD -- this is unambiguously the correct subject/grade/publisher, though note the exact confirmed KICD Drive filename was 'Social Studies Grade 9 - Revised.pdf' and this mirror's own filename/URL string is 'Social-Studies-Grade-9-Design-Formatted-April-2024.pdf' (no explicit 'Revised' in the filename or in the title page text). The document body itself carries a faint diagonal 'DRAFT' watermark on every page despite having an ISBN and 'First published' notice -- this is very likely just a leftover watermark from KICD's internal review/print-proof workflow (the ISBN and ACKNOWLEDGEMENT section describing full stakeholder sign-off indicate this is the finalized published design, not an unapproved draft), but it is flagged here in case a definitively non-watermarked 'Revised' edition later surfaces with content differences. IMPORTANT STRUCTURAL FINDING: the official design has 5 strands, not the 3 the app currently implements (Physical Environment & Population / History & Political Systems / Life Skills in web/src/lib/curriculum.ts). The real strand set is: (1) Social Studies and Career Development, (2) Community Service-Learning, (3) People and Relationships, (4) Natural and Historic Built Environments, (5) Political Developments and Governance -- these do not map cleanly onto the app's current 3 strands; the app's content is missing an entire 'Social Studies and Career Development' strand, an entire 'Community Service-Learning' strand, and the 'Political Developments and Governance' content (constitution, civic engagement, bill of rights, cultural globalisation) is not represented as its own strand either. This is a major coverage gap, not a minor omission. Minor internal inconsistencies noted in the source PDF itself (not this transcription): the 'SUMMARY OF STRANDS AND SUB STRANDS' table (p.x-xi) and the detailed per-sub-strand section headers disagree on suggested lesson counts for a few sub-strands (e.g. Population Structure: 8 in summary table vs '(9 Lessons)' in the detailed section header; Healthy Relationships: 4 in summary table vs '(3 Lessons)' in the detailed header; Management and Conservation of the Environment: 6 in summary table vs '(8 lessons)' in the detailed header). Lesson-count fields are not part of this reference's schema, so these were simply omitted rather than guessed at. The source spells the final sub-strand's name as 'Cultural Globalisation' in the summary table and 'Cultural Globalization' in the detailed section header -- both spellings verbatim from the source, British spelling used here for consistency with the rest of the document.

subStrands.name: Pathway Choices
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify factors to consider in the selection of a pathway
Examine requirements for Social sciences pathway at senior school
Choose a possible track within a pathway at senior school
Appreciate the need for choosing a pathway in senior school
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to learn about career paths?

subStrands.name: Pre-career Support Systems
specificLearningOutcomes: Explore and use support systems for pre-career and other needs
Analyze challenges arising from existing support systems for pre-career and other needs
Design solutions to challenges arising from support systems
Explain the significance of pre-career mapping for individual growth
Appreciate the value of the pre-career support systems
keyInquiryQuestions: Why does a learner need pre-career support?

subStrands.name: Community Service-Learning Project
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify a problem in the community
Design a solution to the identified problem
Plan to solve the identified problem in the community
Implement the plan to solve the problem
Write a report on the concluded project
Appreciate teamwork in addressing community problems
keyInquiryQuestions: What does one consider while implementing a project?
Why is reflection important in a project?
subStrands.notes: This sub-strand is an extended, milestone-based group project (problem identification, solution design, planning, implementation, showcasing/report, reflection -- see Appendix 1 of the source design) carried out over a term against a real community problem, rather than a discrete content topic. It is not naturally amenable to a generated multiple-choice/short-answer practice quiz in the same way other sub-strands are; flagging for an explicit build/decline decision rather than silent omission.

subStrands.name: Socio-Economic Practices of Early Humans
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe the socio-economic practices of early humans in Africa during the Stone Age period
Examine different types of tools used by early humans during the Stone Age period
Illustrate the tools used by early humans during the Stone Age period
Recognise socio-economic practices of the early humans
keyInquiryQuestions: How do socio-economic practices of early humans impact on the modern society?

subStrands.name: Indigenous Knowledge Systems in African Societies
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify types of indigenous knowledge systems in African societies for self-identity
Explain how the indigenous knowledge systems were used for sustainability of life
Use indigenous and modern knowledge systems for effective decision making in life
Appreciate the indigenous knowledge systems in the society
keyInquiryQuestions: How does indigenous knowledge influence on the modern society?

subStrands.name: Poverty Reduction
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain causes of poverty in Africa
Examine the effects of overexploitation of natural resources on poverty in Africa
Apply creative thinking skills to reduce poverty in the society
Recognize the contribution of poverty reduction strategies in society
keyInquiryQuestions: What are the measures taken by African governments to reduce poverty?
How does prudent utilization of resources help to reduce poverty in the society?

subStrands.name: Population Structure
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify sources of population data in a country
Explain factors determining population structure in Kenya and Germany
Construct age-sex population pyramids of developed and developing countries
Determine the significance of population structure in distribution of national resources in a society
Appreciate the differences in population structure between developed and developing countries
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is population structure of a country important?

subStrands.name: Peaceful Conflict Resolution
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain types of peace for sustainable social interactions
Identify barriers to conflict resolution in day-to-day lives
Explore ways of managing emotions in promotion of peace in the community
Apply emotional intelligence for peaceful conflict resolutions in the community
Embrace peace initiatives and agreements at the community level for harmonious living
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote peace in the community?

subStrands.name: Healthy Relationships
specificLearningOutcomes: Explain ways of sustaining healthy relationships in the community
Explore barriers to harmonious relationships
Design strategies to overcome barriers to healthy relationships
Appreciate the need for healthy relationships in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we promote healthy relationships in the community?

subStrands.name: Topographical Maps
specificLearningOutcomes: Describe human activities on topographical maps
Use creative thinking skills to enlarge and reduce parts of topographical maps
Illustrate cross-sections from topographical maps
Appreciate representation of human activities on topographical maps
keyInquiryQuestions: Why are topographical maps important?

subStrands.name: Internal Land Forming Processes
specificLearningOutcomes: Explore the types and causes of earth movements in the environment
Explain the theories of continental drift and plate tectonics in the formation of continents
Illustrate the formation of selected features due to faulting in the environment
Explain the effects of faulting to human activities
Recognise internal land forming processes in shaping the landscape and their influence on human activities
keyInquiryQuestions: How do landforms influence human activities?

subStrands.name: Multipurpose River Projects in Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify selected multi-purpose river projects on a map of Africa
Outline the conditions that led to the establishment of multi-purpose river projects along River Tana
Examine the economic importance of multi-purpose river projects in Africa
Assess challenges facing multi-purpose river projects in Africa
Design solutions to challenges facing multi-purpose river projects in Africa
Recognise the importance of multipurpose river projects in the society
keyInquiryQuestions: How useful are multi-purpose river projects in society?

subStrands.name: Management and Conservation of the Environment
specificLearningOutcomes: Explore factors that lead to degradation of the environment in the community
Describe the effects of environmental degradation in society
Design measures to manage and conserve the environment for sustainability
Apply creative thinking skills in managing and conserving the immediate environment
Acknowledge the importance of managing and conserving the environment
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to conserve degraded environment?

subStrands.name: World Heritage Sites in Africa
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the selected world heritage sites in Africa
Examine importance of the selected world sites in promoting cultural heritage
Design measures to conserve the selected world heritage sites
Apply critical thinking skills in conserving heritage sites within the locality
Value heritage sites in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is it important to conserve the world heritage sites?

subStrands.name: The Constitution of Kenya
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify the stages in the constitution-making process in Kenya
Examine the role of parliament in constitution-making process
Explore the role of citizens in constitution-making process
Participate in the constitution-making process in community
Desire to defend and promote the Constitution of Kenya
keyInquiryQuestions: Why is constitution-making process in Kenya important?

subStrands.name: Civic Engagement in Governance
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify individual and collective civic engagement activities in Kenya
Illustrate the role of political parties in democratic governance
Outline positions vied for in a general election in Kenya
Exhibit values that promote ethical civic engagement in the community
keyInquiryQuestions: How does civic engagement promote good governance in the country?
How can we participate in democratic processes in the society?

subStrands.name: Kenya's Bill of Rights
specificLearningOutcomes: Explore Kenya's Bill of Rights for mutual social well-being
Examine human rights of special groups for promotion of social justice and inclusivity
Apply the bill of rights for harmonious living
Develop assertiveness necessary in standing up for human rights
Cultivate empathy and solidarity with special groups in society for mutual social responsibility
Embrace respect for human rights in society
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we protect the special groups in the community?
subStrands.notes: 'Special groups' in the source design specifically means the elderly, refugees, and migrants (named explicitly in the suggested learning experiences and non-formal activities lists).

subStrands.name: Cultural Globalisation
specificLearningOutcomes: Identify cultural elements and practices that have acquired a global recognition and status
Examine African cultural practices in promoting a common humanity
Explore ways of preserving cultural elements that promotes global citizenship
Enumerate factors that promote healthy cultural relationships and global interconnectedness
Appreciate values and cultural elements which promote responsible global citizenship
keyInquiryQuestions: How can we preserve aspects of cultural globalization in the community?
What are the merits of cultural globalisation?
